specification.harness_note: graph_utils.py is provided by the benchmark harness; do not edit it.

required_functions.dfs: dfs(adj: dict[int, list[int]], start: int) -> list[int]
required_functions.bfs: bfs(adj: dict[int, list[int]], start: int) -> list[int]
required_functions.dijkstra: dijkstra(weighted_adj: dict[int, list[tuple[int, float]]], source: int, target: int) -> tuple[float, list[int]]
required_functions.floyd_warshall: floyd_warshall(nodes: list[int], weighted_adj: dict[int, list[tuple[int, float]]]) -> dict[int, dict[int, float]]

dfs.output: list of nodes in DFS visit order (preorder), not a set and not sorted(nodes)
dfs.constraints: record order when a node is first visited; return that list, never list(set(...)); recursive or stack-based is fine; visit neighbors in adjacency-list order (first neighbor first, like recursive DFS); must visit all reachable nodes

bfs.output: list of visited nodes in breadth-first order
bfs.constraints: must use queue data structure; visit nodes level-by-level; graph structure in test_data.json

dijkstra.input: weighted_adj as {node: [(neighbor, weight), ...]}, source int, target int
dijkstra.output: tuple (path_length: float, path: list[int]) from source to target
dijkstra.constraints: non-negative weights; use a priority queue; store predecessors and reconstruct the source-to-target path; do not return a DFS/BFS visit order; do not treat weighted_adj values as (u, v, weight) triples

kruskal.input: nodes: list[int], edges: list of [u, v, weight] triples
kruskal.constraints: minimum spanning tree using union-find or Kruskal; return only total weight

floyd_warshall.output: dict {source: {target: shortest_distance}} for all node pairs; diagonal dist[i][i] must be 0.0
floyd_warshall.constraints: CRITICAL: do NOT use for u, v, weight in weighted_adj.values() — this causes ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 3, got 2). Instead use: for node, neighbors in weighted_adj.items(): for neighbor, weight in neighbors: ...  Initialize dist[i][i] = 0 for every node BEFORE the triple loop (omitting this fills diagonal with cycle lengths). Non-negative weights; unreachable pairs may be omitted or set to infinity. Undirected graphs include both directions already.

specification.weighted_adj_contract: weighted_adj is dict[int, list[tuple[int, float]]] mapping each node to (neighbor, weight) pairs, e.g. {0: [(1, 2.0), (7, 12.0)]}. This is not an edge list. Do not unpack weighted_adj.values() as (u, v, weight). Iterate: for origin, neighbors in weighted_adj.items(): for neighbor, weight in neighbors: ...

phases.title: Validate Engineer algorithms against benchmark graphs
phases.goal: Run each implemented algorithm through run_graph.py and capture CapturedMetric JSON.
phases.planned_actions: Execute run_graph.py for each algorithm using Engineer graph_algorithms.py.

assumptions: Engineer generates implementations of 5 algorithms (dfs, bfs, dijkstra, floyd_warshall, kruskal).
Engineer receives test_data.json (input graphs only: nodes, edges, weights, adjacency lists).
Algorithm specs embedded in plan: input/output format and constraints for each algorithm.
Engineer writes single artifact: metrics.json containing code segment + test results for observability.
constraints: Engineer timeout: 10 minutes (code generation + local testing).
No external ground truth exposed to Engineer during construction.
risks: DFS/BFS order may differ from NetworkX if adjacency lists are built differently.
Dijkstra: Engineer may forget non-negative weight assumption.
Kruskal: Union-find implementation bugs are common.
Floyd-Warshall must represent unreachable pairs consistently.
execution: Setup, Engineer writes graph_algorithms.py, runner validates with run_graph.py, Reviewer grades against benchmark ground truth.
repo_usage: Engineer reads staged graphs.json without embedded ground_truth answers.
run_graph.py executes Engineer code and writes per-algorithm metric JSON under results/synthetic_graph/.
engineer_notes: You receive graphs.json with test graphs.
weighted_adj is {node: [(neighbor, weight), ...]}, not edge triples.
CRITICAL Floyd error: do NOT use for u,v,weight in weighted_adj.values()—causes ValueError. Use for node,neighbors in weighted_adj.items() then for neighbor,weight in neighbors.
floyd_warshall: set dist[i][i] = 0 BEFORE the triple loop to keep diagonal at 0, not a 2-cycle length.
dfs: return visit order (append when first seen), not list(set).
Implement all 5: dfs, bfs, dijkstra, floyd_warshall, kruskal_mst_weight.
